look_here_first: Check the leaves first: willow oak has long, narrow, unlobed willow-like blades with smooth margins and a tiny terminal bristle. Then check the small acorns in shallow saucer-like cups.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Texas native principally eastward in bottomland habitats; reviewed draft documents no confirmed project target-zone counties.

best_field_traits: narrow linear-lanceolate unlobed leaves, willow-like in outline
entire margins with a minute bristle at the leaf tip
small acorns held in shallow saucer-shaped cups; mature in two seasons

comparisons.key_distinctions: Water oak (Q. nigra) typically has broader wedge- or spatula-shaped leaves, often with a shallowly three-lobed tip. Black willow (Salix nigra) has finely toothed leaf margins, alternate narrow leaves and catkins rather than acorns. Shingle oak (Q. imbricaria) has broader, oblong entire leaves.

diagnostic_image_plan: leaf close-up showing entire margin and minute terminal bristle
small acorn with shallow saucer-like cup
